outcome: Setup > Delegation: list the delegations the backend shows and add one from its own lists (contract mock only)
acceptance_criteria: **Both boards pass.** `SCR-13-desktop-delegation` at 1440 and `SCR-13-mobile-delegation` at 390: `pass: true`, coverage after exceptions 100, visual ≥ 90 (a D-83-style waiver only if the design engineer signs one). — verify: the commands; `round-<N>/fidelity/scores.txt`.

**Exceptions limited.** Each entry in `fidelity-exceptions.json` has `role`, `name`, `category`, `reason`, `approved_by` (`"builder proposal, pending design engineer"` until signed) and maps to a Conflicts number; none covers a value the data supplies (name, role, date, reason, status). One fidelity run per round. — verify: file content; build.md.

**List from data.** With `default`, desktop shows FROM, TO, DATES, REASON, STATE with "Kemi Adebayo · PMO Lead", "Femi Ade · PMO Lead", "18–25 Nov 2026", "Annual leave", "Upcoming", and the ended row; phone shows "Kemi Adebayo → Femi Ade", "PMO Lead · 18–25 Nov 2026 · Annual leave" and the tag. A row without `ends` shows "Unknown"; a row without `reason` or `role` draws nothing there; status comes only from `status` (a test with a past-dated `scheduled` row still shows "Upcoming"). — verify: `tests/setup-delegation.test.tsx`; page at 1440 and 390.

**Add control only on `can_add: true`.** `readonly` (no `can_add`) and a fixture with `can_add: false` show no panel, no button and no disabled placeholder; `default` shows them. The same fixture gives the same controls for personas `admin`, `finance_lead` and `ceo`; nothing reads `me.roles`. — verify: component tests; `grep -n "roles" frontend/src/features/setup/Delegation*.tsx frontend/src/features/setup/useDelegation*.ts` finds no read of `/me` roles.

**No list of its own.** From, To and Authority offer exactly the backend's options in its order, none pre-selected; there is no free-text input for a person or authority; a test that edits the DOM to add an option or dispatches a change to an unlisted value results in no PUT (the submit takes values only from the lists). No string naming a role, authority or person appears in `src/features/setup/Delegation*` or `useDelegation*`. — verify: component tests with a recording `fetch`; `grep -nE "PMO Lead|Finance Lead|Admin|Kemi|Femi|Ada|Chika" frontend/src/features/setup/Delegation*.tsx frontend/src/features/setup/useDelegation*.ts` returns nothing.

**From follows `from_options`.** `single` shows From as read-only "You" and sends no `from_person_id`; `authority` (one option) shows it as text; `default` (two) shows a `Select` and sends `from_person_id` of the chosen one. — verify: component tests.

**To pairing.** In `default`, To is disabled with "Choose who is delegating first." until From is chosen; choosing Kemi lists only Femi, choosing Ada only Chika; changing From clears To. In `single` (no `for_person_id`) To lists every returned option. — verify: component tests.

**Authority.** No field and no `authority` in the body for `default`; read-only line and the single value sent for `single`; a required `Select` with no default for `authority`. Rows with `authority` show "Authority: <label>". — verify: component tests.

**Write request.** A valid add sends exactly one PUT `/api/v1/setup/delegation` with the CSRF header and a body that validates against the overlay `delegation_body`: `expected_revision` = the read's `revision`, `delegate` = the option's `person_id`, `starts`/`ends` as `YYYY-MM-DD`, `reason` trimmed or absent, no `idempotency_key`, no extra keys. A double click sends one. — verify: component tests; `setup-delegation-mock.test.ts`.

**Format checks only.** Missing To, an invalid date, or Ends before Starts shows the message under the field and sends nothing; a past Starts date or any other rule is sent as is. — verify: component tests.

**Success re-reads.** On 200 the first page is re-read, the new row appears from the re-read (not from the 200 body), the polite notice reads "Delegation added: …", focus moves to the new row (or the table heading when no `delegation_id`), the form clears. — verify: component test and e2e.
**422.** With `psl_mock_delegations_save=invalid`, the top message and the messages under To and Ends show, focus goes to To, entries stay. — verify: component test and e2e.
**409.** With `stale`, the list is re-read, the stale sentence shows, entries stay, the next press sends the new `revision`; no automatic resend (fake timers 60 s: one PUT). — verify: component test.

**Uncertain write.** `uncertain`: never "added"; after the re-read, "It was not added. You can add it again." and Add enabled. `uncertain_written`: the new row is listed, the "list changed" warning shows, Add is disabled with its reason and only "Start again" re-enables an empty form. A failed re-read locks the form with "Try again" (read only). — verify: component tests; e2e reads the mock state (one row added in `uncertain_written`, none in `uncertain`).

**Access.** 401 on read or write → signed-out with `next=/setup/delegation`; persona `pm`/`none` or `forbidden` → the not-open view, no names, no further call; 403/404 on the PUT → the backend message, list re-read; `/me` without `setup` → no delegation call at all. — verify: component tests with a recording `fetch`.

**No claimed effect, no agent.** The page contains no text saying a delegate can act, approve or has gained anything, other than the board's note and hint (Conflicts 4); there is no agent, suggestion or generated text. — verify: `grep -niE "can now|now able|has been given|granted" frontend/src/features/setup/Delegation*.tsx` returns nothing; component test of `document.body.textContent` after a success.

**Phone add form.** At 390, "Add delegation" opens the Drawer sheet "Add a delegation" with the same fields, messages and outcomes as desktop; Escape and Cancel close it and return focus to the button; after success the sheet closes and the new card is shown. (Pending Conflicts 1.) — verify: e2e at 390.
**Paging.** `many`: 20 rows, Show more appends the next 20 then 5 and the end message; a failed page keeps loaded rows with the problem callout. — verify: component test.

**Accessibility.** No axe violations (`wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22aa`) at 1440 and 390 on default, the open phone sheet, the 422 state, the uncertain warning, empty, readonly and not-open; no sideways scroll at 390; visible focus; 44px targets on phones (D-92c); every field labelled, the Dates fieldset has a legend; errors announced; status words in text, not colour only; no animation under `reducedMotion: 'reduce'`. — verify: `e2e/setup-delegation.spec.ts`.

**Mock matches the contract.** `setup-delegation-mock.test.ts`: every fixture validates against the generated E-DELEGATIONS 200 schema plus the overlay; the check order; CSRF; persona rule; the 422s for an unlisted delegate, authority and from; 409; success bumps `revision`; reset clears. — verify: `cd frontend && npx vitest run tests/setup-delegation*.test.* tests/mock-contract.test.ts`.

**Contract not extended.** `git diff --stat` shows no change in `frontend/src/api/**`, `apps/**`, `architecture/**`, `design/**`, protected paths, or existing fixtures; every overlay field is a contract proposal in build.md. — verify: `git diff --stat`; build.md.

**Existing behaviour kept.** `tests/setup*.test.*`, `shell.test.tsx`, `tests/components/**`, `e2e/setup.spec.ts`, `e2e/setup-templates.spec.ts` pass with no assertion removed or loosened; the other reserved tabs still render `ReservedTab`. — verify: `delivery/checks.sh`; the e2e command above.

**build.md evidence.** Commands and results, both scores, every exception with its Conflicts number, every contract proposal, the held items and the D-DELEGATION-VIEW limits in the PR description. — verify: file content.

risk.rationale: High. The screen sets who may act for whom (identity and authority), and v7's own D-DELEGATION-VIEW is a proposal, D05 is open and no approver is named, so a wrong default or a derived-from-role control would grant authority. That is why every control follows the backend's response, and why SURFACES include auth and security (INV-ACCESS, no self-approval, authority ceiling). It is contained: only two boards, frontend and mock only (frontend/src/features/setup, frontend/mock), no backend and nothing released, so the damage a mistake can do is limited to the mock until the backend developer enforces the rules. PRODUCT-ACCEPTANCE is required: the add form and the authority wording are a business rule PSL must see, and the phone add form and the From and To narrowing go beyond what the boards draw.

findings.summary: The mock's "no `can_add` → 403" step cannot be reached with the shipped fixtures, and no test covers it. The only fixture without `can_add` is `readonly`, and it has no options, so every add from it fails earlier with a 422 at the delegate check. Expected: the check-order step exists and is tested. Actual: dead code at `frontend/mock/delegations.mjs:151`; build.md (AC 21) admits this. Because of the spec's order, a view-only caller probing the mock also gets a 422 or 409 instead of a 403. That is acceptable for a mock, but the backend developer should know it is a choice to confirm. Fix: in `setup-delegation-mock.test.ts`, add a test that drives `saveDelegation` against a `default`-shaped fixture with `can_add` removed (for example, a `readonly_options` scenario or a fixture override that only the test can use), and assert the 403. Or record the order (403 after the 409) as a backend question in build.md.

findings.summary: The frontend and the mock pair To options differently in two cases. (a) When `from_options` is absent but `for_person_id` is present, the frontend shows the whole `delegate_options` list (`DelegationForm.tsx:61-62`). The mock's `delegatesFor(data, undefined)` then accepts only unpaired options (`frontend/mock/delegations.mjs:97-101`), so every option offered gets a 422. (b) In a mixed list, the mock still accepts options without `for_person_id`, while the frontend drops them (exact match). Only backend values are ever sent and the backend's 422 decides, so this does not break authority. But the mock does not model what the page offers. Fix: make `delegatesFor` use the frontend's exact match, and list "pairing with no From list" as an open question in build.md's contract proposals. The spec does not define that case.

On a 409 whose re-read fails without losing access, the page still shows "This changed while you were working. The list has been reloaded; check it and add again." The list was not reloaded, and the page keeps the old revision (`DelegationView.tsx:135-137`, `useDelegationAdd.ts:42-43`). Nothing unsafe follows: the next press gets another 409. But the sentence is untrue. Fix: when `outcome.page` is an `ApiError`, show the backend message, or a "couldn't reload the list" sentence with the read's retry.

findings.summary: **Problem.** With exactly one entry in `from_options[]`, the read-only From shows that person, but `from_person_id` is not sent. The overlay schema defines an absent `from_person_id` as "absent means the caller" (`frontend/mock/proposals/setup.json`, delegation_body.from_person_id; G-SCR13A-1 "defaults to the caller"). **Concrete case, `authority` scenario.** The person signed in is admin Ada Okafor. The page shows "From: Kemi Adebayo · PMO Lead" and narrows To to Kemi's paired delegate. It then sends `{expected_revision, delegate: 'P-FEMI', authority, ...}` with no From. A backend that follows the proposed contract would record Ada → Femi, not Kemi → Femi. The success notice still reads "Kemi Adebayo to Femi Ade" when it falls back to the form summary. So the page implies an identity and an eligibility pairing that the request does not ask for. The mock hides this because, against its own schema text, it falls back to the single option (`frontend/mock/delegations.mjs:133-134`). The test locks the behaviour in (`frontend/tests/setup-delegation.test.tsx:365`, body without `from_person_id`). Code: `frontend/src/features/setup/DelegationForm.tsx:100` (`if (fromOptions.length > 1 && fromPerson) body.from_person_id = ...`). The spec line in Contract/E-DELEGATION ("sent only when From came from `from_options[]` with two or more choices") causes this, so the spec writer should note the correction. **Fix.** Whenever From is drawn from `from_options[]` (one or more entries), send `from_person_id = fromPerson.person_id`, so the request names exactly the person the screen shows. In the mock, treat an absent `from_person_id` as the caller (the `is_you` row) and not as the single option. Update the `authority` test to expect `from_person_id: 'P-KEMI'`, and add a mock test showing that a single-option add without `from_person_id` is recorded from the caller.

A new mock test shows that a request without From is recorded as `{name:'Ada Okafor', is_you:true}`, and the Kemi→Chika combination is refused. The round-2 build.md says these tests fail on the round-1 code.
